text:
FTR we also switched git strategy from `rebase` to `merge`  to mitigate git conflict issues and also configured all components to use the `--no-wrap`  flag with `gettext` to be in sync with R Core.
Sebastian also applied a patch that source string references are actually excluded from PO files (and kept only in POT files), so that will heavily decrease the risk of future conflicts.
and we have manually also synced current SVN state to the Weblate git to heal all the diversions from the past 3+ yrs :crossed_fingers:

thanks <@U01N3ET8N82> :blush:

there was a related discussion around <https://r-contributors.slack.com/archives/C0210D7EN1X/p1776636877415289?thread_ts=1750070821.690539&cid=C0210D7EN1X|https://r-contributors.slack.com/archives/C0210D7EN1X/p1776636877415289?thread_ts=1750070821.690539&cid=C0210D7EN1X> -- but my main motivation for the switch was to reduce the risk of conflicts (as advertised in the weblate docs as "the safest method", although I think the also in-place "drop source string line-number references from the PO files" helps much more with that) and to help walk back the git history when needed, as that was sometimes rather mysterious in same cases :zipper_mouth_face:

attachments.fallback:
[April 19th, 2026 3:14 PM] daroczig: thanks for looking into this!

hm, I don't recall why we (or probably I at that point) decided to go with rebase over merge, but it does have some advantages -- the most important one being: "upstream is authoritative".
while resolving the git conflicts, we could always be sure that upstream is the source of truth and we should prefer that. keeping the git log linear with frequent (automated) updates from upstream mostly worked fine in the past years, except for a few edge cases -- and while I understand that this is super frustrating and I feel sorry for that, but it's not trivial for me to decide we should switch, so I recommend let's think about the consequences of switching from rebase to merge strategy, then well document this process and make the switch if that seems a brighter path :+1:

one huge con against rebase is that we never actually push back to the upstream so we maintain a crazy divergent branch for a long time .. and yeah, when we need to babysit the rebase process, that actually goes through all the thousands of commits from weblate. switching to merge can mitigate some of that as the past doesn't need to be replayed, while git conflicts would still occur similarly, and the same problem could still hit us, so it's not a silver bullet.
